description:
FORGE CYBER LAB 🚀

Innovate. Build. Explore.

We are passionate about AI, software development, data science, cybersecurity, and space exploration.

For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we're building EARTHWISE AI, an intelligent dashboard using NASA data to explore climate change and environmental trends.

Looking for: Python developers, AI enthusiasts, web developers, UI/UX designers, data analysts, and environmental science enthusiasts.

Beginners with creativity and a willingness to Learn.
summary: EarthWise AI is a free, no-login climate intelligence app built for the challenge "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" It finds real climate trends in NASA data and tests whether they are significant. Using ten years of NASA POWER records (2015–2025) for 172 Pakistani cities, it visualizes how temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind and solar radiation have changed over time, and answers the detective's questions — what is changing, where, by how much, and is it significant? — with Sen's slope and the Kendall tau test. For Lahore, for example, mean air temperature drifted down by about 1.3 °C per decade, but with p = 0.52 the data do not show a clear trend, and the app says so honestly. Around this core, the app adds live weather and air quality (Open-Meteo / CAMS), a whole-Pakistan map, and plain-language daily advisories for health, farmers and the best hours to be outdoors — so the science reaches the people who need it.
details: What it does. EarthWise AI is a live web app with 8 pages: Overview (live weather, AQI and trend at a glance), Climate Analytics (10-year NASA POWER history, Sen's slope, Kendall p-value, monthly and 12-month rolling charts, seasonal anomalies, 10-year outlook with 95% confidence interval), Air Quality (US AQI gauge, PM2.5/PM10, ozone, NO2, CO, 24-hour PM2.5 chart), Weather & Maps (7-day forecast, satellite imagery, and a tappable map of 172 Pakistani cities), Daily Advisory (health verdict, farmer advisory, rain warning, crop planting guide, body-strain estimate and best-hours planner), AI Assistant (answers only from the loaded data), Risk & Outlook (composite screening score) and Data & Downloads (real datasets as CSV). How it works. Built in Python 3.12 with Streamlit. Historical climate comes from the NASA POWER Daily Point API; live weather and forecast from Open-Meteo; live air quality from the Open-Meteo Air Quality API (CAMS); satellite tiles from NASA GIBS. Trends are computed with the Theil–Sen estimator and tested with the Kendall tau test; the 10-year outlook is a straight-line Sen-slope extrapolation with a 95% confidence band. The app is deployed on Streamlit Cloud and the source code is public on GitHub. Benefits. A farmer deciding when to sow wheat, a parent deciding whether children should play outside in smog, a student checking whether their city's climate is really changing — all get plain-language answers from real data, free, with no login, on a phone. The app never invents data and never overstates a trend: when the evidence is not significant, it says so. Tools and languages. Python 3.12, Streamlit 1.63, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Plotly, GitHub, Streamlit Cloud. AI disclosure. The demo video's narration was generated with AI text-to-speech; all visuals in the video are real screenshots of the live app — no AI-generated imagery.
